decks.module: What you carry and when to report
decks.domain: License laws, license types and identity verification

cards.front: What must every driver in New Jersey carry while driving?
cards.back: Anyone driving in New Jersey must carry a valid license, a valid probationary license, or a validated New Jersey permit, and must also carry valid insurance and registration cards.

cards.front: Who must ride along when you drive on a validated New Jersey permit?
cards.back: A driver using a validated New Jersey permit must always have an appropriately licensed driver along.

cards.front: If the driver manual and a statute or regulation disagree, which one governs?
cards.back: When the manual and a statute or regulation disagree, the statute or regulation is what governs.

cards.front: How long do you have to tell the MVC about a new address after you move?
cards.back: After moving, a motorist has one week to report the new address to the MVC, and this rule also covers people moving out of the state.

cards.front: How long do you have to report a legal name change to the MVC?
cards.back: A legal name change, such as through marriage, divorce or a court order, must be reported to the MVC within two weeks.

cards.front: Which reporting deadline is one week and which is two weeks?
cards.back: An address change must be reported within one week of moving, while a legal name change gets two weeks; the two deadlines are easy to swap.

cards.front: How long does a new resident with a valid out-of-state license have to apply for a New Jersey license?
cards.back: A new resident holding a valid out-of-state license must apply for a New Jersey license within sixty days, or before the old license expires if that is sooner.

cards.front: What is the newcomer deadline for a commercial driver license, and what happens to the old license?
cards.back: The newcomer deadline for a commercial driver license (CDL) is thirty days, and the out-of-state license is surrendered once the New Jersey license is received.

cards.front: How long may a motorist drive on a valid license from another country?
cards.back: A motorist whose valid license comes from another country may drive on it for up to one year.

cards.front: Compare the newcomer windows for a regular license, a CDL, and a license from another country.
cards.back: A new resident with a regular out-of-state license has sixty days to apply in New Jersey, a CDL holder has only thirty days, and a driver with a license from another country may drive on it for up to one year.

decks.module: New drivers, decals and the CDL path
decks.domain: License laws, license types and identity verification

cards.front: What program must someone who has never held a driver license complete?
cards.back: Anyone who has never held a driver license must complete the Graduated Driver License (GDL) Program, which phases in privileges after a stretch of supervised driving.

cards.front: What must a license applicant under eighteen present?
cards.back: A license applicant under eighteen must present a consent form that a parent or guardian has completed and signed.

cards.front: Which young drivers must display reflective GDL decals, and where do they go?
cards.back: Drivers under twenty-one holding an examination permit, special learner's permit or probationary license must show two reflective GDL decals, supplied by the MVC, on the vehicle's license plates.

cards.front: What must a driver already hold before applying for a CDL?
cards.back: Commercial vehicle drivers face tougher testing than car or motorcycle drivers and must already hold a valid basic New Jersey license before they apply for a CDL.

cards.front: What is the minimum CDL age, and what limits apply to CDL holders under twenty-one?
cards.back: CDL applicants must be at least eighteen, and those under twenty-one may drive only inside New Jersey and cannot receive HAZMAT or passenger endorsements.

decks.domain: License laws, license types and identity verification

cards.front: How and where has every New Jersey license and non-driver ID been produced since the security upgrade?
cards.back: Since a two thousand twenty-one security upgrade, every New Jersey license and non-driver ID, Standard or REAL ID, is produced at a secure central facility that uses facial recognition to fight identity theft.

cards.front: What do you receive at the transaction, and how does the actual card reach you?
cards.back: At the transaction you receive a temporary license or ID that is valid for thirty days, and the card itself is mailed to you, with delivery expected within thirty days.

cards.front: What format of card do motorists under twenty-one receive, and how long are licenses and IDs valid?
cards.back: Motorists under twenty-one receive a vertical-format license or non-driver ID card, and licenses and IDs are valid for four years.

cards.front: How long is the temporary paper license good compared with the mailed card?
cards.back: The temporary paper license or ID lasts thirty days, while the mailed card itself is valid for four years.

cards.front: When does an endorsement expire, and which endorsement is the exception?
cards.back: An endorsement expires together with the license it is on, except Hazmat, which requires retesting every two years.

cards.front: How does a Hazmat endorsement differ from most endorsements?
cards.back: Most endorsements simply expire with the license, but a Hazmat endorsement must be retested every two years.

cards.front: How is the charge figured when an endorsement is added to an existing license?
cards.back: When an endorsement is added to an existing license, its charge is prorated for the time left until the license expires.

cards.front: What fee does a motorist pay when returning to a Licensing Center after one year to upgrade the license?
cards.back: A license-chart footnote says a motorist who must return to a Licensing Center after one year to upgrade the license pays a prorated fee, usually nineteen dollars and fifty cents Standard or twenty-nine dollars REAL ID.

cards.front: What penalties can follow altering a license, obtaining one by fraud, or presenting an altered one?
cards.back: Altering a license or ID, obtaining one by fraud, or presenting an altered one can bring loss of driving privileges, fines up to one thousand dollars, imprisonment, or a combination.

decks.domain: License laws, license types and identity verification

cards.front: In the license chart, what do the letters K, V, R and C stand for?
cards.back: In the license chart, K means the Knowledge test, V the Vision test, R the Road test and C the Commercial test.

cards.front: What does the basic automobile license cover, and what are its minimum and permit ages?
cards.back: The basic automobile license covers every MVC-registered Class D vehicle except motorcycles, with a minimum age of eighteen and a permit age of sixteen.

cards.front: What are the ages and fees for the probationary automobile license?
cards.back: The probationary automobile license has a minimum age of seventeen with a permit at sixteen, a permit fee of ten dollars plus four dollars for red reflectorized decals, and a sixty-three dollars license fee.

cards.front: How do the minimum ages of the basic and probationary automobile licenses compare, and what permit age do they share?
cards.back: The basic automobile license requires age eighteen and the probationary automobile license age seventeen, yet both list a permit age of sixteen.

cards.front: What fees and tests does the chart list for the basic automobile license?
cards.back: The basic automobile license chart lists a ten dollars permit fee and license fees of twenty-four dollars Standard or thirty-five dollars REAL ID, and requires knowledge, vision and road tests.

cards.front: What vehicles and classes does a commercial driver license cover, and what does it add?
cards.back: A commercial driver license covers large trucks, buses and similar vehicles in Classes A, B and C, carries a one hundred twenty-five dollars permit fee and adds a commercial test.

cards.front: What does a Class E motorcycle license cover, how is it issued, and what is its minimum age?
cards.back: A motorcycle license (Class E) covers most vehicles with fewer than four wheels and is issued either as its own license or as an M endorsement on a basic New Jersey license, with a minimum age of seventeen.

cards.front: Who may get a moped license, and who does not need one?
cards.back: A moped license is for unlicensed motorists aged fifteen or older and is not required for anyone who holds a Class A, B, C, D or E license.

cards.front: What is an agricultural license for, who may get it, and how long does it last?
cards.back: An agricultural license is only for farming, may be granted to people aged sixteen to seventeen, and lasts four years or until the holder gets a basic license at eighteen.

cards.front: What are the starting ages for the moped license and the agricultural license?
cards.back: A moped license starts at age fifteen, while an agricultural license is granted at sixteen to seventeen and is for farming only.

cards.front: Who needs a boat license, and what must every power-vessel operator show when applying?
cards.back: A boat license is for people sixteen or older running a motorboat on fresh, non-tidal waters, and every power-vessel operator must show a Boating Safety Certificate when applying.

decks.domain: License laws, license types and identity verification

cards.front: What does a Standard license applicant provide?
cards.back: A Standard license applicant provides proof of a Social Security or Taxpayer Identification Number (or an affidavit of ineligibility), one proof of New Jersey address and six points of identification.

cards.front: What mix of documents does a Standard license applicant need?
cards.back: A Standard license applicant needs a mix of documents: one or more primary documents, one or more secondary documents, a total of at least six ID points, and proof of a New Jersey home address.

cards.front: Name the primary proofs of identity accepted for a Standard license.
cards.back: Primary proofs of identity for a Standard license include a US birth certificate, a US passport or passport card, a passport from the applicant's country of citizenship, and a digitized New Jersey license or non-driver ID.

cards.front: When does a foreign-issued photo driver license count toward identity?
cards.back: A foreign-issued photo driver license counts toward identity only when it is presented together with another government-issued document.

cards.front: For a Standard license, how far past expiration may a primary or secondary document be?
cards.back: For a Standard license, no primary or secondary document may be more than three years past its expiration date.

cards.front: How many one-point documents may a Standard applicant count toward the six points?
cards.back: Standard license applicants may count no more than two one-point documents toward their six points.

cards.front: What separate note does the Standard document chart carry for CDL applicants?
cards.back: The Standard document chart carries a separate note that CDL applicants must prove US citizenship or lawful permanent resident status.

decks.domain: License laws, license types and identity verification

cards.front: What language rule applies to identification documents?
cards.back: Identification documents must be written in English or be accompanied by an approved translation.

cards.front: What physical condition must identity documents be in?
cards.back: Identity documents must be unlaminated originals or certified copies, in English, and carry the required state or municipal seal.

cards.front: What may the MVC do if documents conflict or look altered?
cards.back: If documents conflict the MVC may ask for more, and it may refuse any permit or license application when a document looks altered, false or invalid.

cards.front: What must a Standard license proof of residency show, and what are examples?
cards.back: A Standard license proof of New Jersey residency must show the applicant's name and home address, for example a utility or credit card bill up to one year old or a pay stub up to six months old.

cards.front: For a Standard license, how old may address proofs be, and how many are needed?
cards.back: For a Standard license, address proofs such as a bank statement, a utility or credit card bill, or first class government mail may be up to one year old, and only one address proof is needed.

cards.front: Which two New Jersey documents both show an address but cannot be submitted together?
cards.back: A valid New Jersey license and a valid New Jersey vehicle registration both show an address, but they cannot be submitted together as address proofs.

cards.front: Which two financial documents cannot be submitted together, and what may be blacked out?
cards.back: An ATM or debit card and a bank statement cannot be submitted together, and financial details on documents may be blacked out.

decks.domain: License laws, license types and identity verification

cards.front: What does a REAL ID license applicant provide?
cards.back: A REAL ID license applicant provides two proofs of New Jersey address, one proof of the full Social Security number and six points of identification, including proof of lawful presence in the United States.

cards.front: What are REAL ID Steps I, II and III?
cards.back: REAL ID Step I is the two address proofs, Step II is one proof of the full Social Security number, and Step III is the six points from primary and secondary documents.

cards.front: How many documents do you select from the REAL ID primary list?
cards.back: For REAL ID you select one and only one document from the primary list, for example an unexpired US passport or passport card, or a certified US birth certificate.

cards.front: May paper documents used in REAL ID Steps I and II also count in Step III?
cards.back: Paper documents already used in REAL ID Steps I and II may also serve as secondary options in Step III when they appear on that list.

cards.front: How many one-point secondary documents may count in REAL ID Step III?
cards.back: In REAL ID Step III no more than two one-point secondary documents may be used toward the six points.

cards.front: How recent must REAL ID address proofs be?
cards.back: For REAL ID the address windows are tighter: a utility or credit card bill from the past ninety days, a bank or credit union statement from the past sixty days, or first class government mail from the past six months.

cards.front: On the REAL ID secondary list, which standard photo licenses and non-driver IDs count?
cards.back: On the REAL ID secondary list an unexpired standard photo license may come from New Jersey or any state, but an unexpired standard non-driver ID card counts only if New Jersey issued it.

decks.module: Name changes and Social Security proof
decks.domain: License laws, license types and identity verification

cards.front: What must you show if your current legal name differs from your birth certificate?
cards.back: If your current legal name differs from your birth certificate, you must show legal proof of the change, such as a certified marriage or civil union certificate, divorce decree, or court order linking the names.

cards.front: When does a divorce decree support going back to a previous name?
cards.back: A divorce decree supports going back to a previous name only if it lists both the married and previous names and permits the return to the previous name.

cards.front: What can a marriage or civil union certificate prove, and what can a divorce decree support?
cards.back: A marriage or civil union certificate can be used only to prove a change of last name, while a divorce decree supports only a return to a previous name that it lists.

cards.front: What may an applicant file if they cannot get a Social Security number and have no ITIN?
cards.back: An applicant who cannot get a Social Security number and has no ITIN may file an affidavit, which must be notarized or signed in front of an MVC agency employee.

cards.front: What must you bring if the Social Security Administration cannot verify your number?
cards.back: If the Social Security Administration cannot verify the number given on the application, the applicant must bring a document showing the full name and full number, such as a Social Security card or a W-two from the past year.

recaps.module: What you carry and when to report

recap_hooks.text: Carry your license or permit, your insurance card and your registration card, and a permit driver always needs a licensed driver along.
Report a move within one week and a legal name change within two weeks; newcomers get sixty days, CDL holders thirty, and a foreign license works for up to one year.

recaps.module: New drivers, decals and the CDL path

recap_hooks.text: Never licensed means the GDL Program, under eighteen means a signed parent consent form, and under twenty-one GDL drivers show two decals.
A CDL needs a basic New Jersey license first, and CDL holders under twenty-one stay inside the state.
You leave with a paper license good for thirty days, and the mailed card lasts four years.
Endorsements end with the license, except Hazmat, which is retested every two years.
The basic license starts at eighteen and the probationary at seventeen, and both permits start at sixteen.
Mopeds start at fifteen, and the farming-only agricultural license is for ages sixteen to seventeen.
A Standard applicant brings a Social Security or tax number, one address proof and six points of identification.
Only two one-point documents can count, and no document may be more than three years expired.
Documents must be in English or translated, original or certified, and the MVC can ask for more when they conflict.
A Standard address proof can be up to a year old, but a license and a registration cannot be paired as address proofs.
REAL ID is two address proofs, one full Social Security proof, then six points.
Choose exactly one primary document, and expect tighter date windows for REAL ID address proofs.

recaps.module: Name changes and Social Security proof

recap_hooks.text: A marriage certificate proves a new last name, while a divorce decree supports a return to a name it lists.
No Social Security number and no ITIN means a notarized affidavit.

merges.justification: sec01-F33 restates the sec01-F12 REAL ID document combination (two address proofs, one full Social Security proof, six points of identification) as one model; its accepted wording writes the model with plus symbols that cannot be spoken as a card back, so the sec01-F12 card carries both facts and the sec01-F33 detail is taught in its exam item and lesson.
